title: BitFold quantized-model onboarding and regression-correlation playbook
creator: Anita Rao
description:
Purpose: define an operationally deterministic onboarding path for low-bit (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) model artifacts ("BitFold" variants) and build a regression-correlation harness that ties functional and perf deltas back to the model, quantization parameters, sequence-distribution, and infra profile. This ticket covers the ingestion contract, baseline fingerprinting, telemetry keys, automated delta attribution, and a minimal human-in-loop signoff flow for publishing a quantized variant to the catalog.

Why: teams keep deploying low-bit builds that pass micro-benchmarks but cause downstream tail-latency regressions or accuracy regressions for specific prompt shapes. We need a reproducible pipeline that produces a clear verdict (pass/warn/fail) and produces targeted signals for rollback or conservative rollout (region/model-family gating).
acceptance_criteria: Onboarded pipeline accepts BitFold artifacts and emits a standardized metadata blob (model_name, base_checkpoint, quant_strategy, bitwidth, layerwise-scale-metrics, tokenization-fingerprint, build_commit, container-sha).

Baseline fingerprint created from reference dataset: sequence-length buckets (short/med/long), batch sizes, and representative prompt shapes. Baseline includes p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint, and eval-quality metrics (perplexity / top-k shift).
Regression-correlation harness computes per-bucket deltas vs baseline and attributes primary driver tags (eg. kernel-switching, KV-cache-growth, unaligned-matmul).
Automated gate publishes one of: PASSED, WARN, FAILED. WARN cases create a human review task (links to perf dashboard and failed traces).
Playbook documents rollout knobs (canary %) and automated fallback policy mapping to release channels (hosted -> dedicated -> private).
A smoke CI job runs nightly to re-validate published BitFold variants on a matrix of instance types; failures trigger the regression ticket template with pre-filled telemetry.
steps: 1) Artifact intake: extend manifest schema to include quant_metadata.* fields and enforce schema validation in intake lambda.
2) Baseline generation: run the new fingerprint harness on the upstream FP32 pinned checkpoint to create a controlled baseline for later delta calculation.
3) Telemetry contract: add telemetry keys (quant_variant, quant_bits, quant_backend, kernel_path_id, seq_bucket, batch_size, perf_label) to ingestion pipeline and backend traces.
4) Regression-correlation engine: implement comparison runner that highlights top 3 contributing deltas and maps them to triage templates.
5) Runbook + UI: author a console-level summary card with verdict, delta heatmap by sequence bucket, and deep-link to sample traces and failing prompts.
6) Automation+Rollout: wire verdict to the publish pipeline so PASSED artifacts go to 'staged' channel, WARN require manual approval, FAILED get rejected.
7) Nightly revalidation: schedule 02:00 UTC job across a 3-region matrix; correlate drift across regions and GPUs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting to the reference dataset can miss customer prompt shapes. Mitigation: include a "wildcard" set of customer-sanitized prompts and require minimum coverage across prompt families.
Risk: Telemetry volume spike from additional tags. Mitigation: sample keys at 1% for high-frequency routes and use histogram aggregation for token-level metrics.
Risk: False positives from infra variance. Mitigation: require at least 3 independent runs across different nodes (or a resample window) before marking FAIL.
implementation_notes: - New manifest keys: quant_metadata.schema_version (v1), quant_metadata.backend_name, quant_metadata.bit_spec, quant_metadata.per_layer_scale_hash.
- Fingerprint store: use existing artifact-store under /fingerprints/bitfold/{model}/{variant}/{date}.json and expose via signed URL for reviewers.
- Delta attribution heuristics: compare kernel selection logs, op-count diffs, and KV-cache size deltas. Prototype uses weighted-sum attribution (weights: latency 0.6, memory 0.3, quality 0.1).
- CLI tool: `redwood quant-validate` provides a preflight check to run locally for SEs before artifact upload.
